title: Present simple and present continuous for the future
subtitle: The sun rises at 5:16 / Are you seeing the doctor?
summary: Use the present simple for timetabled future events and after time and conditional conjunctions, and the present continuous for firm intentions.

lesson.heading: Present simple for timetabled events
lesson.text: For future events that are part of a timetabled or programmed arrangement or routine, either the present simple or **will** is usually possible. We prefer the present simple for fixed, unchangeable events.

examples.text: **Does** the sale **finish** on Thursday or Friday?

examples.note: more likely than The sun will rise ...

lesson.heading: But not for looser arrangements or predictions
lesson.text: We avoid the present simple for less formal or less routine arrangements, and for predictions. Instead we use **will**, **be going to** or the present continuous.

examples.text: **Are** you **staying** in to watch TV tonight, or **are** you **coming** dancing?
examples.wrong: Do you stay to watch TV tonight, or do you come

examples.text: It's only a problem in Britain now, but it **will affect** the rest of Europe soon.
examples.wrong: but it affects the rest of Europe soon

lesson.heading: Present simple, not will, in time clauses
lesson.text: After conjunctions such as **after, as soon as, before, by the time, when, while** and **until** we use the present simple to refer to the future.

examples.text: When you **see** Ben, tell him he still owes me some money.
I should be finished by the time you **get** back.
examples.wrong: by the time you will get back

lesson.heading: And in conditional clauses
lesson.text: The same goes for conditional clauses with **if, in case, provided** and **unless**, and after **suppose, supposing** and **what if** at the beginning of a sentence.

examples.text: Provided the right software **is** available, I should be able to solve the problem.
I'll bring some sandwiches in case we **don't find** anywhere decent to eat.
Suppose we **miss** the bus - how will we get home?
examples.note: or Suppose we missed ... - the past simple has a similar meaning

examples.text: What if the train**'s** late? Where shall I meet you then?
examples.note: or What if the train was late?

lesson.heading: Present continuous for firm intentions
lesson.text: For planned future events the present continuous and be going to are often interchangeable. The present continuous says that we have a firm intention or have definitely decided to do something, even if nothing has been arranged yet.

examples.text: **Are** you **seeing** the doctor again next week?
examples.note: or Are you going to see ...?

examples.text: **I'm not asking** Tom to the party.
examples.note: or I'm not going to ask ...

lesson.heading: Two things the present continuous can't do
lesson.text: We don't use the present continuous for the future when we predict activities or events we have no control over - we can't arrange those - or when we talk about permanent future situations.

examples.text: I think it**'s going to rain** soon.
Scientists say that the satellite **won't cause** any damage when it falls to Earth.
People **are going to live** / **will live** longer in the future.
Her new house **is going to have** / **will have** three floors.

lesson.heading: go and come
lesson.text: Many people avoid **be going to + go / come** and use the present continuous forms of go and come instead.

examples.note: rather than I'm going to go to town ...
rather than Are you going to come ...?

lesson.text: After when, until, provided, unless, in case, suppose and what if, never use will - the present simple already points to the future.

exercises.prompt: I think I'll take an umbrella in case it ___.
exercises.explanation: In case introduces a conditional clause, so the present simple refers to the future.

exercises.prompt: The concert ___ at 7:30, not 7:15 as it says in the programme.
exercises.explanation: A fixed, timetabled event: the present simple is the natural choice (will start is also possible).
Correct. For a fixed, unchangeable event the present simple is more likely than will rise.

exercises.prompt: Provided it ___ raining, we'll go for a walk this afternoon.
exercises.explanation: Provided introduces a conditional clause, so the present simple, not will.

exercises.prompt: *A:* I'm not sure how I'll get to the concert. *B:* We can take you. We ___ you up at eight.
exercises.explanation: This is an offer, decided at the moment of speaking, so will.

exercises.statement: It's only a problem in Britain now, but it affects the rest of Europe soon.
exercises.explanation: ... but it will affect the rest of Europe soon. The present simple is not used for predictions.

exercises.prompt: By the time you ___ this letter, I should be in New Zealand.
exercises.explanation: By the time is a time conjunction, so the present simple points to the future.

exercises.prompt: I'm sorry I can't come for dinner. I ___ to York tonight.
exercises.explanation: A definite arrangement you have already made: the present continuous (or am going to drive).

exercises.prompt: I've heard that BWM are building a new factory in Ireland. If you look on their website, you ___ a lot of information about it.
exercises.explanation: This is about ability - you'll be able to see it - so will, not a present tense.

exercises.prompt: The high-speed rail link ___ the journey time between the cities significantly.
exercises.explanation: A permanent future situation, so will or be going to - never the present continuous.

exercises.prompt: Ask a friend whether the plan for tonight is a night in front of the TV or a night out dancing.
exercises.answer: Are you staying in to watch TV tonight, or are you coming dancing?
exercises.explanation: These are informal arrangements, so the present continuous - not the present simple.

exercises.prompt: Present simple or will + infinitive? (... marks the gap.)

items.text: We ... our exam results on the 20th August.
Alex ... our cats while we're away next week.
Unless my parents ... me some money, I won't be able to go on holiday this year.
We ... Mariam when she leaves, but she says she'll keep in touch.
Supposing I ... to upload a video to YouTube? How do I do that?
It is unlikely that the government ... the court's decision.
